S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar and its .integration is accessed without optional chaining. WHY: When destinationCalendar is null, undefined, or empty, mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration throws a TypeError, breaking event creation. HOW: Use optional chaining: mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar".

S2.label: bug
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: When externalCalendarId is undefined, the fallback searches event.destinationCalendar for an entry whose externalId equals undefined, which can never match. WHY: updateEvent loses the previous default of event.destinationCalendar.externalId and may call calendar.events.update with an undefined calendarId; deleteEvent falls back to "primary" instead of the intended host calendar. HOW: Fall back to the first destinationCalendar entry, e.g. event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId. The same fix applies to deleteEvent at lines 315-317.

S3.label: bug
S3.suggestionContent: WHAT: Office365 createEvent still has the old one-argument signature and always uses event.destinationCalendar[0]. WHY: CalendarManager now calls createEvent(calEvent, credential.id), and for collective bookings it expects the credential's matching destination calendar to be selected; Office365 ignores credentialId and writes every host's event to the first destination calendar. HOW: Accept credentialId and select the destinationCalendar entry whose credentialId matches, then use that entry's externalId.

S4.label: bug
S4.suggestionContent: WHAT: Lark createEvent was not updated to accept credentialId and still reads event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId. WHY: With multiple destination calendars, Lark events for additional hosts are created in the wrong calendar because the implementation cannot select the calendar matching the credential in use. HOW: Update the signature to (event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number) and select event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId).

S5.label: bug
S5.suggestionContent: WHAT: The slug and requestedSlug metadata conditions were inverted from !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED. WHY: Non-billing/self-hosted instances no longer store the organization slug, breaking routing, while billing-enabled instances store both slug and requestedSlug, bypassing the verification flow. HOW: Restore the original conditions: write slug when billing is disabled and requestedSlug only when billing is enabled.

S6.label: bug
S6.suggestionContent: WHAT: The recurring-event cancellation branch iterates over all user calendar credentials inside a loop over every calendar reference. WHY: For collective recurring bookings with multiple calendar references, each calendar event is deleted once per reference, producing redundant API calls and 404/not-found errors. HOW: Use only the credential from the current reference (the already-resolved calendarCredential) instead of looping over bookingToDelete.user.credentials.

S1.label: security
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: Any attendee of a booking is authorized to add arbitrary guests. WHY: An attendee who knows the bookingId can invoke addGuests and inject new recipients into a meeting they do not own, bypassing organizer control and exposing meeting links/calendar events to unintended parties. HOW: Restrict addGuests to the same principals as bookingsProcedure (organizer or collective participant) or gate attendee access behind an explicit organizer/team-admin permission.

S2.label: bug
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: The team permission check requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. WHY: `isTeamAdmin` already returns true for ADMIN or OWNER roles; `isTeamOwner` returns true only for OWNER, so pure team admins are incorrectly denied permission to add guests. HOW: Change the operator from `&&` to `||` so either an admin or an owner is authorized.

S3.label: bug
S3.suggestionContent: WHAT: `sendAddGuestsEmails` receives the raw `guests` input instead of the deduplicated `uniqueGuests` list. WHY: If the request includes an email that is already an attendee, that attendee is filtered out of `uniqueGuests` and no new record is created, but the email logic still treats it as a new guest and sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. HOW: Pass `uniqueGuests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails`.

S4.label: security
S4.suggestionContent: WHAT: The blacklisted-guest check is case-sensitive. WHY: `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` is lowercased before comparison, but the submitted `guest` email is compared verbatim, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing (e.g. `BadEmail@example.com`) is accepted. HOW: Normalize the submitted email to lowercase before comparing against the lowercased blacklist.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: refreshOAuthTokens is called with credentialId instead of the user's id. WHY: The helper's third parameter is documented as userId, so the credential-sync endpoint receives a credential primary key as calcomUserId and cannot look up the correct user. HOW: Pass credential.userId as the third argument.

S2.label: bug
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed property names [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] which evaluate to a fixed string such as '[object Object]', not a pattern for arbitrary keys. WHY: When credential sync is enabled every token response will fail this schema because it lacks a property literally named by that string, causing parseRefreshTokenResponse to throw 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned'. HOW: Replace the computed keys with a passthrough object schema or z.record.

S3.label: bug
S3.suggestionContent: WHAT: The result of parseRefreshTokenResponse (a SafeParseReturnType wrapper { success, data }) is stored directly as the credential key. WHY: The next load calls googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key), which expects the parsed credential shape at the top level, not an object nested under a data property; this breaks the credential after any refresh. HOW: Extract tokenResponse.data before storing.

S4.label: bug
S4.suggestionContent: WHAT: After refreshOAuthTokens, the code reads res?.data, but when credential sync is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response object which has no .data property. WHY: token becomes undefined, so token.access_token throws a runtime error and the calendar refresh crashes. HOW: Normalize the helper output or fall back to parsing the Response JSON.

S5.label: bug
S5.suggestionContent: WHAT: The code refreshes the access token, writes the new token to the database, then constructs the jsforce Connection using the old credentialKey.access_token. WHY: The refresh is effectively wasted and the connection may be initialized with an expired access token. HOW: Use the refreshed token data when building the connection.

S6.label: security
S6.suggestionContent: WHAT: The webhook secret is compared with the !== operator. WHY: String comparison short-circuits on the first mismatching byte, allowing an attacker to brute-force the secret one byte at a time via timing analysis. HOW: Compare secrets with crypto.timingSafeEqual after length check.

S7.label: bug
S7.suggestionContent: WHAT: The handler reads the credential with findFirst and then decides to update or create, but the Credential model has no unique constraint on (userId, appId). WHY: Two concurrent webhook requests for the same user and app can both observe no credential and both insert, producing duplicate credential rows. HOW: Add a @@unique([userId, appId]) constraint and use prisma.credential.upsert with a composite key, or wrap the create in a retry on unique-violation.

S8.label: performance
S8.suggestionContent: WHAT: The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no timeout or abort signal. WHY: If the external endpoint hangs, the calling calendar/video request also hangs indefinitely, consuming workers and potentially blocking user-facing operations. HOW: Add an AbortController with a timeout and handle abort errors.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: The catch block increments retryCount for any error in the try block, not only for SMS scheduling failures. WHY: Failures from `prisma.profile.findFirst`, `getBookerBaseUrl`, or other unrelated setup can mark a reminder for deletion even though Twilio was never attempted. HOW: Wrap only the `twilio.scheduleSMS` call and the successful update in try/catch, or restructure so retryCount is incremented only when scheduling itself fails.

S2.label: bug
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: The deleteMany second OR branch deletes WorkflowReminder rows with retryCount > 1 without filtering by method. WHY: This cron job is scoped to SMS reminders, but the new condition would also delete email or other-method reminders if any future code increments their retryCount. HOW: Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the retryCount branch so both disjuncts are method-scoped.

S3.label: performance
S3.suggestionContent: WHAT: The cron job's deleteMany queries `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` on WorkflowReminder, but there is no index on the new retryCount column. WHY: The OR branch has no method filter, so the planner cannot use the existing `method, scheduled, scheduledDate` index for it; on a large table this can become a sequential scan every cron run. HOW: Add an index on `retryCount` (e.g., `@@index([retryCount])` or `@@index([method, retryCount])`) in schema.prisma and the migration.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: Backup code verification compares the user-supplied code without normalizing case. WHY: Generated backup codes are lowercase hex, so a user who types an otherwise valid code in uppercase is rejected as incorrect. HOW: Lower-case the stripped input before comparing, e.g. `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "").toLowerCase()`, and apply the same normalization in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts line 61.

S2.label: security
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new backup-code authentication branch does not itself verify the user's password. WHY: Password verification is gated by `!credentials.totpCode`, so an attacker who knows a backup code can bypass the password by also sending any non-empty totpCode and authenticate successfully. HOW: Verify the password inside the backup-code branch (or move password verification before the second-factor branches) before consuming the backup code.

S3.label: bug
S3.suggestionContent: WHAT: The clipboard writeText call is not awaited and its errors are not handled. WHY: The success toast is shown immediately even if the browser rejects the copy (permission denied, insecure context, etc.), misleading the user and leaving an unhandled promise rejection. HOW: Await the clipboard call and only show the toast on success, or catch errors and show an error toast.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: Tests assert equality between flat Prisma.sql template literals and nested Prisma.sql compositions returned by the service. WHY: The service builds compound conditions by interpolating Prisma.Sql fragments into other Prisma.sql templates (e.g., buildFilterConditions and buildOrgAuthorizationCondition), producing Sql objects whose values array contains nested Sql objects; Jest toEqual compares enumerable strings/values properties, so the flat expected literals will not match the nested actual values and the tests will fail. HOW: Assert on the emitted SQL text instead, e.g., expect(conditions.text).toEqual(expected.text), or use a helper that normalizes Prisma.Sql to its flattened text/values before comparison.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: Protocol-relative URLs such as '//cdn.example.com/foo' are rewritten to 'http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/foo'. WHY: The code strips all leading slashes from any href/src starting with '/' and then prefixes the base host, so protocol-relative links break and point at the wrong host. HOW: Skip or separately handle protocol-relative URLs; only rewrite single-slash relative paths.

S2.label: bug
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: The scheduled job calls i.content.scrub without checking whether i.content exists. WHY: Many RSS/Atom feeds provide only a description or summary, so i.content is nil and the job raises NoMethodError, aborting the entire feed import. HOW: Guard against nil content, falling back to an empty string or the item's description/summary.

S3.label: bug
S3.suggestionContent: WHAT: The script immediately calls comments.appendChild(iframe) without verifying that document.getElementById('discourse-comments') returned an element. WHY: If the host page omits the container or loads the script before the element exists, comments is null and appendChild throws, breaking other scripts on the page. HOW: Guard the appendChild call with an if (comments) check.

S4.label: bug
S4.suggestionContent: WHAT: TopicEmbed.import appends the 'Imported from' footer to the input contents string using <<, mutating the caller's object. WHY: In-place mutation can corrupt reused strings and raises RuntimeError when the caller passes a frozen string; it also makes the function's side effects unpredictable. HOW: Build a new string instead of mutating the parameter.

S5.label: bug
S5.suggestionContent: WHAT: fetch_http calls SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase without verifying the setting is present. WHY: If feed polling is disabled and embed_by_username is blank, the retrieve job raises NoMethodError on nil.downcase instead of failing gracefully. HOW: Return early when the username setting is blank, matching the guard in PollFeed.

S6.label: performance
S6.suggestionContent: WHAT: perform_retrieve invokes Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously inside the current job. WHY: This blocks the Sidekiq worker while the entire feed is fetched and every item is imported, even though only the requested embed_url is needed. HOW: Either look up only the specific embed_url in the feed, or enqueue PollFeed asynchronously and let the loading page continue polling.

S7.label: performance
S7.suggestionContent: WHAT: poll_feed calls open(feed_url).read without a timeout and iterates rss.items without any limit. WHY: A slow or unresponsive feed can hold a worker indefinitely, and a very large feed can consume excessive memory and time importing every item. HOW: Add a read timeout to open and cap the number of items processed per run.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: `update` and `destroy` fetch a host with `.first` and use it without checking for nil. WHY: A request with a non-existent ID causes `NoMethodError` when `save_host` assigns `host.host = ...` or when `destroy` calls `nil.destroy`, returning a 500 instead of a clean 404. HOW: Use `EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id])` (raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound → 404) or guard nil and `render_json_error` / head 404.

S2.label: security
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: The migration interpolates values from `site_settings` directly into an INSERT statement. WHY: An admin who previously set `embeddable_hosts` to a value containing a single quote can inject arbitrary SQL that runs with full database privileges during migration. HOW: Use parameterized SQL or escape each host value before interpolation.

S3.label: performance
S3.suggestionContent: WHAT: `record_for_host` queries with `lower(host) = ?` but the table has no index on `host`. WHY: This lookup runs on every embedded request, and as the allowed-hosts list grows it degrades to a full table scan. HOW: Add an index on `host` in the migration, ideally `lower(host)` if the database supports expression indexes, or a standard btree index with case-insensitive comparisons in the query.

S4.label: bug
S4.suggestionContent: WHAT: The fabricator file contents are swapped between `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. WHY: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines `:embeddable_host`, while category-related fabricators were moved to `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`, making the file names misleading and breaking the convention that a fabricator file defines the model named in its filename. HOW: Move the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` fabricators back to `category_fabricator.rb`, and keep `:embeddable_host` in `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`.

S5.label: bug
S5.suggestionContent: WHAT: `TopicEmbed.import` now passes `category: eh.try(:category_id)`, which becomes nil when no embeddable host matches the URL. WHY: Previously the default `SiteSetting.embed_category` was always used; feed polling and import scripts that call `import` directly can now create topics with no explicit category, changing behavior for URLs that do not match a configured host. HOW: Fall back to the uncategorized category or the old default when `eh` is blank, matching the controller's blank-category handling.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: The `align-items` mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment`, which is not a valid CSS property. WHY: IE10/11 ignore this declaration; while the correct `-ms-flex-align` is also present, the invalid line is dead code that contradicts the mixin's intent of covering all prefixes and may mislead future maintainers. HOW: Remove the invalid `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` line.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: A second `downsize` class method with a different arity overrides the first, because Ruby redefines singleton methods rather than overloading by arity. WHY: The existing caller `app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14` passes `(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`, which the surviving signature maps as `dimensions=100` and `opts=100`, causing `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for 100:Integer` when `downsize_instructions` reads `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]`. HOW: Remove the duplicate and keep a single `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` method; update `resize_emoji.rb` to call `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, '100x100', opts)`.

S2.label: bug
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new downsize loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize` but discards its return value. WHY: `OptimizedImage.convert_with` returns `false` when ImageMagick fails or raises an exception, so a failed resize leaves the original oversized tempfile intact and `Upload.create_for` still stores it, allowing uploads that exceed `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. HOW: Check the return value and abort or skip the upload when downsizing fails, e.g. `break unless OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` inside the loop and validate the final size before creating the upload.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: The `totalPages` computed property uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which overcounts by one when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`. WHY: With 100 members and a page size of 50 it reports 3 total pages instead of 2, so `showingLast` stays false on the real last page and `next()` navigates to an empty page. HOW: Replace the formula with `Math.ceil(this.get('user_count') / this.get('limit'))`.

S2.label: performance
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: The `members` action now reads `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` without enforcing a maximum. WHY: The previous implementation capped automatic groups at 200 members per request; that cap is gone, so any user who can view a group can request an unbounded number of records (e.g. `?limit=9999999`), causing a large DB query and memory load. HOW: Cap the limit to a reasonable maximum such as `limit = [[params[:limit].to_i, 200].min, 1].max` or equivalent.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but leaves the underlying hash empty, so every method other than `[]` (e.g. `each`, `keys`, `defaults`, `map`) sees an empty collection. WHY: This violates the I18n::Locale::Fallbacks/Hash contract; any future caller that iterates or inspects `I18n.fallbacks` will get no locales even though `I18n.fallbacks[:en]` returns a fallback chain. HOW: Delegate storage to a real Hash by calling `super` in `[]` and populating defaults explicitly, or do not inherit from Hash and instead implement only the small interface I18n::Backend::Fallbacks actually needs (e.g. `def [](locale); ... end`).

S1.label: security
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: tagDeviceUI sets the local cache before the database write succeeds, so a failed CreateOrUpdateDevice leaves a cached entry that suppresses limit checks for 29 minutes. WHY: after the first ErrDeviceLimitReached rejection, retries from the same device hit the cache and skip the store, allowing anonymous authentication to bypass the configured device limit. HOW: move a.localCache.SetDefault to after a successful a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice(ctx, device) return, or invalidate the cache on error.

S2.label: bug
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: CreateOrUpdateDevice checks CountDevices and then performs the insert/update in separate, non-atomic steps. WHY: concurrent requests can both see count < deviceLimit and both insert new devices, allowing the number of stored devices to exceed the configured anonymous device limit. HOW: wrap the count check and write in a single transaction with an appropriate isolation level, or enforce the limit with a single set-returning query.

S1.label: performance
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: The write lock is held while performing blocking file I/O or an HTTP request to the CDN. WHY: Every concurrent request that needs web assets is serialized behind that single I/O operation, causing a startup/request-time bottleneck. HOW: Perform the asset loading outside the lock and only acquire the lock to read or update the cache pointer; alternatively use sync.Once for initial population and an atomic pointer for reads.

S2.label: bug
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: After acquiring the write lock, the function does not re-check whether another goroutine already populated the cache, and it assigns `result` to the cache even when `result` is nil due to an error. WHY: A later goroutine that failed to load assets can overwrite a previously successful cache entry with nil, causing every subsequent non-Dev request to re-read the manifest and defeating the cache. HOW: Add a double-checked read after acquiring the write lock and only update the cache when the load succeeded.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: NewMetricsMiddleware returns a middleware closure that reuses the same *MetricsMiddleware instance and mutates its `next` field. WHY: Decorating more than one client with the returned middleware overwrites the chain and, because the metrics are already registered on the same registerer, a second factory use can panic with duplicate metric registration. HOW: Inside the closure create a new *MetricsMiddleware (or a shallow copy of the registered metrics struct) with its own `next` pointer, registering the metrics only once at factory construction time.

S2.label: performance
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: QueryData and CallResource look up the plugin target from the registry twice per request (once for size and once for duration). WHY: The duplicated registry lookup doubles the work on every plugin request for the two instrumented endpoints. HOW: Resolve the target once per method and pass it into both instrumentPluginRequestSize and instrumentPluginRequest, or add a helper that records size and duration with a single lookup.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: When Storage.Create fails, the code records a legacy-duration metric instead of a storage-duration metric. WHY: This corrupts the dual_writer_legacy_duration_seconds histogram with values from the unified store and makes the storage-error path invisible in the storage metric. HOW: Replace `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` with `d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...)` in the error branch.

S2.label: bug
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: When Storage.Update fails, the code records a legacy-duration metric instead of a storage-duration metric. WHY: It misattributes the unified-store error to the legacy store and leaves the storage-duration histogram without an error observation. HOW: Replace `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` with `d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...)` in the error branch.

S3.label: bug
S3.suggestionContent: WHAT: The async legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records a storage-duration metric for the legacy call. WHY: It puts legacy-call latency into the dual_writer_storage_duration_seconds histogram and leaves the legacy histogram without an observation. HOW: Use `d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` inside the goroutine.

S4.label: bug
S4.suggestionContent: WHAT: On successful Delete, the storage-duration metric is observed with `name` as the third label instead of `options.Kind`. WHY: The third histogram label is `kind`; passing the object name creates inconsistent label values across methods and inflates metric cardinality with unique names. HOW: Pass `options.Kind` to match the error path and other methods.

S5.label: bug
S5.suggestionContent: WHAT: The goroutines spawned for async legacy writes are created from the request context using `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`. WHY: The request context is canceled when the HTTP handler returns, so the async legacy write is likely canceled before it completes, defeating mode 3's purpose of writing to legacy as a safety measure. HOW: Detach the goroutine context from request cancellation, e.g. `context.WithTimeoutCause(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), time.Second*10, ...)` so it can run to completion or its own timeout.

S6.label: performance
S6.suggestionContent: WHAT: Every Create, Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection spawns a new goroutine that can live up to 10 seconds with no concurrency limit or backpressure. WHY: Under high write throughput this creates unbounded goroutine fanout and memory growth, especially if the legacy store is slow or times out. HOW: Bound concurrency with a worker pool or semaphore, or use a rate-limited background queue for legacy writes.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: Removing the coarse cacheMu lock at the start of BuildIndex leaves concurrent calls for the same NamespacedResource key unsynchronized. WHY: Two goroutines that reach BuildIndex for the same key (e.g., concurrent Search requests or a Search racing with a watch event via getOrCreateIndex) both create indexes; for file-backed indexes they collide on the same directory, and the second writer overwrites the first in the cache without closing it, leaking the index. HOW: Reintroduce per-key synchronization that still allows different keys to build concurrently—check the cache under a per-key lock/mutex before starting, return the existing index if present, and only write the newly built index if no other builder won the race.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: The SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer is only rendered when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true, but `GrafanaRuleListItem` passes only `promRule` and leaves `rule` undefined. WHY: Clicking the Silence action in the Grafana rule list menu sets `showSilenceDrawer` to true but the drawer never mounts, so users cannot silence Grafana rules from the list view. HOW: Also check the prom rule type, e.g. change the condition to `(rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) || prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(promRule)) && showSilenceDrawer`.

S2.label: bug
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: The `GrafanaRuleListItem` rendered for `origin === 'grafana'` omits the `key` prop, while the `datasource` and `default` branches include `key={key}`. WHY: React will use index-based keys for this list, which can cause component state to be reused for the wrong rule when the filtered list reorders or updates, leading to incorrect actions/links being shown. HOW: Add `key={key}` to `GrafanaRuleListItem`.

S3.label: bug
S3.suggestionContent: WHAT: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` gates `ModifyExport` on `isAlertingRule`, which is true only for alerting rules, whereas the ruler-based equivalent gated it on `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule` (true for all Grafana-managed rules). WHY: Grafana-managed recording rules lose the export action when viewed through the Prometheus-rule list path, breaking feature parity with the ruler-based view. HOW: Change the support flag to `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` or `true` for all Grafana-prom rules, e.g. `[prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule), exportAllowed]`.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: The access-token ID matcher reads the wrong substring and inverts the equality check. WHY: The encoder writes the grant shortcut at indices 4-5 of the prefix, but the matcher reads substring(3, 5) and returns false when it equals the expected shortcut, so the matcher never rejects a token with the wrong grant type. HOW: Change the condition to `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

S2.label: bug
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: The constructor null-checks grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId. WHY: A null rawTokenId is silently accepted, and the error message refers to grantType even though rawTokenId is the value being checked. HOW: Change the fourth requireNonNull to check rawTokenId: `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: The reader thread in the new test catches only Exception, so any Error (e.g., AssertionError, OutOfMemoryError) thrown during concurrent group reads is silently swallowed. WHY: The main thread then asserts caughtExceptions is empty and passes even though the reader thread failed, masking real failures and making the test give false confidence. HOW: Change the catch to Throwable, keep the exception list typed as Throwable, and use assertTrue(caughtThrowables.isEmpty(), ...) so any failure fails the test visibly.

S2.label: bug
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: The test starts a background reader thread but never joins it before returning. WHY: The reader can continue executing groups() calls after the test method ends, during test cleanup or while the next test is running, causing potential flakiness and cross-test interference. HOW: Join the reader thread after setting deletedAll=true, with a reasonable timeout, and fail the test if it does not terminate.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: The HTML tag detector and anchor matcher use case-sensitive regular expressions (`<[a-z]+[^>]*>` and `]*>`) even though HTML element names are case-insensitive. WHY: The OWASP sanitizer canonicalizes tag names to lowercase, so a translation with `text` or `` is not matched by the anchor pre-check and is then normalized by the sanitizer to lowercase, making `sanitized != value` and causing a false-positive "Illegal HTML" build failure. HOW: Compile `HTML_TAGS` and `ANCHOR_PATTERN` with `Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE` (or add `A-Z` to the character classes for tags and `A` for anchors) so the verifier treats HTML case-insensitively.

S2.label: bug
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: `verifySafeHtml` unconditionally throws `RuntimeException` when the computed English base file cannot be read. WHY: Any community translation file that does not have a matching `_en.properties` in the parallel `resources` directory will cause a `FileNotFoundException`, which is wrapped in `RuntimeException` and aborts the entire Maven build instead of reporting a verification message. HOW: Treat a missing English base as a verification message (e.g., "Missing English base file for ...") or fall back to an empty bundle, rather than throwing.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: The provider event listener that disables permissions on role/client/group removal now runs only when the legacy ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature is enabled. S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` and `hasPermission(String)` do not verify that returned `Permission.resourceId` matches the resource being evaluated. UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission filters on `permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId())`, so the same defensive check should be applied here. HOW: Add the resourceId equality guard inside the permission loops in `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, `hasPermission(String)`, and `hasGrantedPermission`.

S1.label: bug

S2.label: bug

S3.label: bug

S4.label: bug

S5.label: bug

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: submit() sums Redis cluster memory info once per flusher process. WHY: iter_cluster_memory_usage returns per-master-node usage for the shared Redis cluster, so summing across N buffers inflates used/available by N and can falsely trigger the hard backpressure pause. HOW: collect memory_info from a single buffer (e.g. next(iter(self.buffers.values())).get_memory_info()) instead of extending across all buffers.

S2.label: bug
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: _ensure_processes_alive() checks isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) before killing a process. WHY: the flusher uses multiprocessing.get_context("spawn"), whose Process class is multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, not multiprocessing.Process (fork on Linux), so the guard is False and dead/hung child processes are never killed before a replacement is spawned, leaking processes. HOW: kill any non-thread process, e.g. check not isinstance(process, threading.Thread) or use hasattr(process, "kill").

S3.label: bug
S3.suggestionContent: WHAT: join() breaks out of the per-process loop as soon as the deadline expires for one process. WHY: remaining later processes are not waited for or terminated, so they can keep running past the shutdown timeout and leak. HOW: continue to the next process instead of break, or at least terminate each process before moving on.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: The `queued` default uses `timezone.now()` as a dataclass default, which evaluates once at class definition time. WHY: Every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` value will share the same stale datetime (when the module was first imported), defeating the purpose of recording when the assignment was queued. HOW: Use `dataclasses.field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance gets a fresh timestamp at creation time.

S1.label: bug

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now extends StatefulDetectorHandler but does not implement the required abstract methods counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, or build_occurrence_and_event_data, so Python treats the class as abstract. S1.label: bug

WHY: Slots that start within working hours but run past the host's end time are accepted, letting a host be booked outside their availability. S3.label: bug
S3.suggestionContent: WHAT: The all-day-unavailable override check compares two dayjs objects with `===` (line 114). S4.label: bug

S1.label: bug

S2.label: bug

S3.label: bug

S1.label: bug

S2.label: bug

S2.label: bug

S4.label: bug

S1.label: bug

S4.label: bug

If the intent is truly to skip failed offsets, move complete_offset out of finally and only call it on success (or add an explicit failure tracker).

S3.label: bug
S3.suggestionContent: WHAT: test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling asserts that no offsets are committed after a processing failure, but the implementation completes offsets for failed items in a finally block and then commits past them. WHY: The test will be flaky/incorrect because both offsets 100 and 101 complete, so get_committable_offsets() will return offset 101 (committed as 102 by commit_offsets). The assertion `len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets` will fail whenever the commit loop wakes up before the assertion. Align the test with the intended semantics: either expect commit offset 102 (move past failures) or change the implementation to not complete failed offsets.

S4.label: performance
S4.suggestionContent: WHAT: FixedQueuePool creates unbounded queue.Queue() instances with no maxsize. WHY: The docstring claims "Natural backpressure when queues fill up", but put() never blocks, so when ingestion outpaces processing the queues grow without bound and can consume unbounded memory. HOW: Pass maxsize=N to queue.Queue() and rely on the blocking put() to apply backpressure, or document that backpressure must come from the upstream Arroyo strategy.

S5.label: performance
S5.suggestionContent: WHAT: OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets() iterates range(start, max_offset + 1) to find the highest contiguous completed offset. WHY: If offsets are sparse (log-compacted topic, skipped filtered messages), the loop runs in O(offset gap) rather than O(backlog), which can become very large and stalls the commit thread. HOW: Sort the tracked offsets and walk the sorted list to find the highest contiguous completed offset, which is O(n log n) in the number of tracked offsets.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: `process_batch` reads `val['end_timestamp_precise']` from a raw `ingest_spans_v1.SpanEvent`, but that Kafka schema only guarantees `end_timestamp`. WHY: Every real span message will raise `KeyError`, crashing the consumer batch. HOW: Construct `Span` using the actual schema field `val['end_timestamp']` (converted to the precise float representation the buffer expects).

S2.label: bug
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: The Lua cap evicts with `zpopmin` on a sorted set scored solely by `end_timestamp_precise`, so older ancestor spans can be removed while their newer descendants remain. WHY: This produces incomplete segments, breaks root-span detection in `flush_segments` (so root timeout is not applied), and contradicts the stated goal of prioritizing spans higher in the hierarchy. HOW: Make the eviction score hierarchy-aware, e.g. by giving each ancestor level a large score bonus so descendants are evicted before their parents.

S3.label: bug
S3.suggestionContent: WHAT: `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` is no longer enforced: `_load_segment_data` dropped the span-count guard and `add-buffer.lua` hard-codes 1000. WHY: Changing the `max_segment_spans` constructor option has no effect, and the cap is now controlled by an undocumented magic number that diverges from the default (1001). HOW: Pass `max_segment_spans` into the Lua script as an argument and evict to that limit, or remove the option if it is intentionally deprecated.
